### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/verify`, touching **38** documentable anchor(s).

**35** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3d9188502e1b07ae70df8b0b5e733fce44a74cfa`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **25** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3d9188502e1b07ae70df8b0b5e733fce44a74cfa` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `cb293614b7a2f843c7f90818b566007e4e72c48f` — the merge of head `870717aca6a06c2faee793d7bd5d155e82251ea5` into base `3d9188502e1b07ae70df8b0b5e733fce44a74cfa`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin cb293614b7a2f843c7f90818b566007e4e72c48f && git checkout cb293614b7a2f843c7f90818b566007e4e72c48f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3d9188502e1b07ae70df8b0b5e733fce44a74cfa 870717aca6a06c2faee793d7bd5d155e82251ea5 && git checkout -B drift-repro 3d9188502e1b07ae70df8b0b5e733fce44a74cfa && git merge --no-ff 870717aca6a06c2faee793d7bd5d155e82251ea5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3d9188502e1b07ae70df8b0b5e733fce44a74cfa
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3d9188502e1b07ae70df8b0b5e733fce44a74cfa` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `870717aca6a06c2faee793d7bd5d155e82251ea5`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #15196 (body and all 18 comments, the #22006 ruling B pointer `6028868506`, the claim `6038279203` and its amendment `6039096736`, the census `6039018686`, the dev report `6041138705` and the seat review `6041196673` included), PR #22100 (body, 20-file list, the net diff of `3d9188502e...870717aca6`), and the 35 check-runs on the head. The local clone at the merge base was read for the engine, writer and guard positions the diff cites. ⛔ Classes, positions and functions only.

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set or public-surface change the diff implies, judged right or wrong.

1. **Read surface — `sys_user_permission_set.permission_set` (`objects/sys-user-permission-set.object.ts`).** `Field.text`, `readonly`, `maxLength: 100`, not required. Every reader of the grant row gains one nullable field. **Right.** The shape is the sibling assignment's `sys_user_position.position` (text, 100, a `sys_*.name`), which is the D4 reference shape; `readonly` keeps the authoring forms off it; NULL on pre-change rows is right because the backfill is S4b, not this stage. ADR-0131 names no column, and the chosen name follows the precedent the PR body cites. The label differs from the id column's, so the two columns are distinguishable in every rendered list.

2. **Insert accept set (`grant-permission-set-name.ts#onInsert` → `#settle`).** Before: any payload carrying the key was refused `400 INVALID_FIELD` for every caller (undeclared key). After: omitted → stamped with the derived name; agreeing → kept; naming any other set → `400 VALIDATION_FAILED`, one `fields[]` entry, `invalid_value` at `permission_set`, a member of the closed ADR-0114 field catalog (no new error code). **Right.** The claim "no write that was accepted before is refused now" holds on the diff: every previously accepted write carried no `permission_set`, the only new refusal paths require a supplied name, and an id-only write whose id resolves nowhere is handed to the engine's own reference check exactly as before. A throwing catalog read propagates (the write is refused rather than landed half-written), which is a store failure handed to the caller, not a verdict.

3. **Update accept set (`#onUpdate`).** The caller's value is judged from `ctx.submitted`, and the stamp is an in-place assignment on `ctx.input.data`. **Right, and the two halves are the engine's own contract:** the hide pass (engine.ts, the #16344 block) names `ctx.submitted` as the channel a submission-reading guard uses — the identity write guard's 403 is the precedent — and a hook assignment is recorded in `hookWrittenKeys`, the one credential the post-hook static strip honours. A middleware stamp would be stripped; the PR measured this. The per-write memo keys on `dispatch.scope`, which the engine binds once on the batch context and carries by identity onto every per-row dispatch (`dispatchPerRowBeforeHooks`), so one catalog read serves a predicate update. `previous` is bound on both update dispatch paths, so the name-only update is judged per matched row against the stored id. A predicate update that writes neither column leaves the name alone, so no backfill rides an unrelated edit.
   **One consequence named, not a defect:** a whole-record write-back that re-points `permission_set_id` AND echoes the stale name is refused `400`, where the engine's lenient idiom alone would strip and restamp. By D4 (the two columns never disagree) and Prime Directive 12 (refuse at the door, no lenient fallback) the refusal is the right side, and the message carries the prescription (omit it, or send the exact name). No shipped writer re-points a grant. Carried to ③ for the Setup edit path.

4. **The unresolvable-id branch.** Non-system caller with a supplied name → refused with the same envelope whether the id names nothing or names another organization's set (pinned on a walled two-organization posture, shape-equal); system writer with a supplied name → kept (seed ordering, census row 23c). **Right.** The catalog read is `ctx.api.sudo()`, which `ScopedContext.sudo` builds as `{ ...context, isSystem: true }` — the `referenceCheckContext` shape, tenant-walled, inside the writer's transaction — never a bare system context. The refusal never echoes the derived name, so a caller learns nothing about a set outside its wall. `classifyFilterToken` refuses a placeholder-shaped id before the read.

5. **Hook placement and lifecycle (`security-plugin.ts`).** Priority 30: after the identity write guard (10, `identity-write-guard.ts`) and the last-administrator guard (20, `last-admin-guard.ts`), before default-priority hooks (100). Verified at those positions. Registered under one `packageId` with no metadata binding, so the `skipAutomations` opt-out cannot bypass it; bound in `start`, unbound in `destroy` through `this.ql`. A composition whose engine exposes no hook registry logs a `warn` naming what is not derived — a functional degradation at the right level. **Right.**

6. **Writers, each writes both columns, and the name is the one the id was resolved by.** Promote (`bootstrap-platform-admin.ts#bootstrapPlatformAdmin`): `PLATFORM_ADMIN_PERMISSION_SET_NAME` beside `seeded[that name]`, where `seeded[ps.name] = row.id` is the row found or created under that name. Reconcile (`auto-org-admin-grant.ts#reconcileOrgAdminGrant`): `grantSetName`, the argument `resolvePermissionSetId` found the own-organization row by (`where: { name }`). Self-registration (`auth-manager.ts#settleSelfRegistrationGrant`): `row.name`, the resolved row's own spelling. RLS persona (`verify/src/rls.ts#provisionRlsProbePersona`): `RLS_PROBE_PERMISSION_SET`, found or created under that name. **All right.** The PR's correction of the claim amendment is verified: `ensure-default-organization.ts` inserts only `sys_organization` and `sys_member`; its grant touches are a trigger predicate and two reads. Writers outside the list (the data door, seed datasets, code outside this repository) get the name from the hook; the dogfood run includes system inserts that carry no name.

7. **Readers unchanged.** No resolver, explain-engine, guard or Setup page is in the file list; `display_title`, `titleFormat` and the Setup related list keep `permission_set_id`. The grant-equivalence golden holds four principal kinds in two postures across the real writers and `resolveUserAuthzGrants`, recorded on the pre-change tree and green on this head. **Right:** S4a changes no principal's grants, which is what the stage plan's "widens: no" means.

8. **Package surfaces.** `@objectstack/plugin-security`'s barrel (`src/index.ts`) does not export the new module; `plugin-auth` and `verify` export nothing new. The publishable change is the column, the hook behaviour and the writers' payloads. **Right.** One pairing named: the `verify` RLS persona now sends `permission_set`, so `@objectstack/verify` pairs with a `plugin-security` that declares the column; the lockstep `minor` on all three packages carries that, and a mixed-version install would be refused loudly (`INVALID_FIELD`), never silently.

9. **Bookkeeping and gates.** `system-context.mdx` row 23c anchors `grant-permission-set-name.ts#settle` and the counts move 114 to 115; the ADR anchor JSON matches the register's shape (`file`, `adrs`, `invariant`); the four `plugin-security` i18n bundles carry the new key with hand-written locale values. Not governed: no path under `docs/adr/`, `.claude/`, `skills/`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` or `docs/NORTH-STAR.md` (`check-governed-merges.mjs` register). Head repository equals base repository. 1,378 changed lines, under the 5,000 threshold. Check-runs on the head: the seven required contexts (`Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Build Core`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`) all `success`; 30 of 35 runs `success`, the two `skipped` (`Console Pin Gate`, `Packed-tarball smoke`) are path-gated and opt-in respectively, with no `.objectui-sha` move in the diff. `Check Changeset` and `Spec property liveness` `success`.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/15196-grant-permission-set-name-column.md`: `minor` for `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/verify`. It names the column, the system-written rule, the `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` / `invalid_value` refusal, the four writers, "no reader uses the column yet" and "nothing to migrate".
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` — line 2 of the PR body and in the changeset body. **Right.** The accept set widens on both doors (a new readable field; a new write key accepted when it agrees), nothing an author could write before is refused now, nothing is removed or renamed, and `packages/spec` is untouched, so no ADR-0087 disposition is owed. `yes` takes at least `minor`; `minor` on all three packages matches what the diff publishes, and the lockstep on `verify` is the pairing named in ①.8.
- Not `skip-changeset`: three released packages change behaviour.

### ③ Boundary flags

The dev report's `open_questions` is empty. Every flag in the PR's acceptance notes, the report's out-of-scope findings, the seat review and the card's carriers is answered below; none is escalated.

1. **Setup related list and `display_title` still show the id** — answered: readers are S5 and C9 by the claim amendment and the stage plan; S4a's "no reader changes" holds on the diff.
2. **No index on `permission_set`** — answered: no reader reads it; S5 brings the index with the reads. The object file is also held by #5082 (index respelling); the regions are disjoint and the later lander merges `main`, as the seat review records.
3. **A `sys_permission_set` row renamed at engine level leaves its grants naming the old name** — answered: the data door refuses renames (ADR-0094), the projector upserts by name, no in-repo writer renames a set row, and the S4b backfill's verification is where a mismatch surfaces. Carrier S4b. Related, named here for that carrier: reconcile and promote write the declared constant while self-registration writes the row's own spelling; under a case-folding collation a hand-renamed row would make the constant disagree with the derived name and the hook would refuse the system write, which reconcile reports as `skipped` / `insert_failed`. No in-repo path renames, so this is bounded to S4b's verification.
4. **A platform writer naming the wrong set is refused and reconcile reports `skipped`** — answered: the writer pins (promote, reconcile both postures, self-registration, RLS persona both branches) and the G1 ablation hold it; the outcome is handed to the caller as a returned value, which the degradation-log-level rule names as delivery, not a degradation.
5. **Test fixtures declaring a minimal grant object without the column** — answered: the one that drives a writer sending the name (`plugin-auth` `find-envelope-limb-removal.test.ts`) now declares it; the eleven others drive no grant writer; `Test Core` is green.
6. **`security-plugin.ts` touched outside the claim amendment's file list** — answered: the registration and teardown only (18 lines); #21908 is a decision card, not in flight; accepted by the seat review.
7. **The create-side `readonly` strip exempts the reserved `sys_` namespace** (a ruled boundary) — answered: the hook is the guard for this column on insert, and the measurement with hooks unbound (a disagreeing name stored verbatim) is what the insert pins stand on. Recorded, no carrier.
8. **Card carriers.** #22006 ruling B (the position-to-permission-set relation keeps reading `sys_position_permission_set` until C3): S4a reads no junction — holds. The `field` sharing-recipient pointer: a record-relative name, outside the grant column — not applicable. The shared-name carrier note: a by-name read question, pinned in S1; S4a derives the name from the id through the row catalog — not applicable. Q2 (the standing ruling keeps the row `active` flag authoritative): the hook does not consult `active` and stamps a grant to a deactivated set like any other; activation stays the readers' row read — consistent.
9. **Reviewer's carrier, not escalated:** a whole-record write-back that re-points the grant's id and echoes the stale name is refused `400` with a prescription (①.3). If the Setup edit form submits readonly columns back, re-pointing a grant through it meets that refusal. Carrier: C9 with S5, the stage that moves the Setup surfaces onto the name column. No ruling is needed: the refusal is loud and names the fix, and no shipped writer re-points a grant.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-15196-s4a-grant-name-column`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WMQprn46CND82KmY8sZWBu`

**VERDICT: PASS**
